To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the capture cross sections of traps at the Si-SiO _{2} interface are temperature-dependent.

the interface trap density and the thermal capture cross section distributions are strongly temperature dependent, that the a.c. conductances are not directly related to the interface trap density but are related to the thermal capture cross sections, that the interface traps are filled in the same way as the bulk traps, that the capture cross sections are not independent of temperature, and that the capture cross-section distributions are not independent of interface trap density.
(1) the capture cross section of interface traps depends on temperature, and (2) this dependence cannot be explained by the standard model, i.e., by a single-phonon process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the temperature dependence of the capture rate constant and the capture cross section for interface traps.
the determination of the capture cross sections of interface states in SiO _{2} /Si systems by DLTS.
the temperature dependence of the capture coefficient and with the energy distribution of the capture cross sections of interface states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the capture cross sections of interface traps cannot be determined by DLTS.
the capture cross sections of interface traps in Si-SiO _{2} systems depend on the temperature and the energy position of traps.
the energy resolved DLTS technique is not a suitable method to measure the thermal capture cross section of interface traps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in addition to the interface trap density, also the thermal capture cross section of the interface trap is an important parameter to be taken into account when studying the interface trap properties of a MOS structure.

, in order to obtain reliable experimental results for the capture cross section, the energy distribution of the traps has to be determined by an energy-resolved technique and the capture cross section should be obtained from the temperature dependence of the emission rate.
the interface trap density and the capture cross section are not constant parameters, but rather depend on the measurement conditions, such as temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when using the a.c. conductivity technique, it is necessary to consider the temperature dependence of the capture process.
a.c. conductancemeasurement techniques should be carefully applied to determine the thermal emission rate of traps in order to avoid erroneous results.
the capture cross sections of interface traps are not temperature-independent and that their values are not necessarily the same as those of bulk defects in the same material system.
